title: Finish my browser task
description: Ends your task with its verified outcome, and with keep closes its pages in the same call: pass keep [] to close every page the task opened, or name the pages to leave open for the person.
guidance: Pages the person opened, other tasks' pages and pages a wizard, run, question or a wall the person must pass holds are never closed (heldPages lists them). A wall never blocks the finish: a verification challenge you hold closes with its page, or goes to the person on a page you keep. Without keep, a 60-second countdown the person can stop closes the task's pages. For an ordinary task, dsagent.page.close on its last page also ends it as succeeded; a continue task (taskMode continue or step reports) ends only by this call. Name one page of the task. Open work must be resolved first: another call of the task, its wizard or run, an assist, or a question waiting for the person; the refusal (TARGET_BUSY, TASK_WORK_OPEN) names it and the way out. Without a finish, ten idle minutes end an unattended task as interrupted, never as successful. compileRun true also returns the task's verified steps as replay scripts for dsagent.page.script: keep them beside the person's skill and run them next time.

inputSchema.description: The page identifying your task, its verified terminal outcome, and the pages to keep.

pageContextId.description: A page reference belonging to the task you are finishing.

status.description: The outcome you verified for this task: succeeded, failed or cancelled (completed is accepted as succeeded).

items.description: A pageContextId of this task to leave open.

keep.description: Close the task's other pages now: [] closes them all, listed pages stay open for the person. Omit for the 60-second countdown instead.

compileRun.description: Return run: this task's verified page steps compiled into Playwright-style scripts for dsagent.page.script, one per page, typed values as input fields. Save them beside the skill you followed and run them next time instead of planning each step again.

outputSchema.description: The recorded terminal outcome of this task, and what keep closed.

status.description: The terminal status recorded for this task.

closedPages.description: With keep: how many of the task's pages this call closed.

keptPages.description: With keep: the kept pages that are this task's and still open; a name that is not one is left out.

run.description: With compileRun: the task's verified steps as replay scripts.

pages.description: One script per page, in order: open url with dsagent.page.open, then run source with dsagent.page.script and input.

url.description: The address the script starts on.

source.description: The script, Playwright-style; review it before reuse.

input.description: Input fields with the values typed in this run; sensitive fields are empty.

notes.description: Steps the scripts leave to single calls or could not name.

siteKnowledgeAsk.description: Present (on the reply that hands the task its data, and on the finish) when this task used a site no earlier run taught you about and recorded nothing for it. If you learned how the site works, call dsagent.site.knowledge.record once per site with its pageContextId: it still takes a record for 5 minutes, at the revision of its last observation. Optional; never data.

note.description: What to do with the sites.

sites.description: The sites, each with the last page the task used there.

revision.description: The revision of its last observation, for entries that name a targetId.

heldPages.description: With keep, when any: the task's pages left open because something still holds them, such as a sign-in or verification wall the person must pass. They stay for the person; do not close them.
